pages.title: Short-Faced Bear
pages.text: The short-faced bear ($(o)Arctodus simus$()) is an extinct bear that lived across North America during the Pleistocene, until about 12,000 years ago.$(br2)It was one of the largest carnivorous land mammals of the Ice Age, with long legs that gave it great height at the shoulder.$(br2)Despite its name, its snout was not unusually short; its deep muzzle only made it look that way. Its closest living relative is the spectacled bear.
